title: Build observed-exit real LLM scalping paper soak
description: PR #377 current-head evidence shows the real LLM no-order scalping probe is instruction-compliant but its per-cycle paper_trade exits are synthetic: each trade is closed from the same market snapshot with slippage/fees, so it cannot prove profitability or live-trial readiness. Latest artifact: /private/tmp/neuratrade-paper-live-evidence-20260519175421-llm-readiness/ai-scalping-probe-20260519175421.json. Summary: completed_cycles=20, signal_quality_coverage=1, valid_contract_cycles=20, llm_degraded_cycles=0, actionable_cycles=19, paper_trades=19, paper_wins=0, paper_losses=19, paper_net_pnl=-0.145828891108891105550648, paper_live_trial_readiness.ready=false. Implement a real LLM paper soak that carries LLM-opened paper positions across observed future market snapshots until hold period/SL/TP exit, persists evidence, and feeds the strict readiness verifier before any real-money or tightly capped live/testnet signaling.
close_reason: Implemented observed-exit real LLM paper probe support in PR #377: signal snapshots, carried paper positions, observed_paper_* metrics, readiness based on observed exits/open positions, and --require-observed-live-trial-ready. Smoke evidence is recorded; profitability remains failing under parent NeuraTrade-00a.

title: Reject implausible perfect scalping paper soak evidence
description: The final merged-runtime Bitget paper/no-order soak for PR #374 reported 123 closed trades, 123 wins, 0 losses, and 0 drawdown. That is too good to trust as acceptance evidence because the paper simulator can effectively turn every eligible signal into an immediate realized winner. Add a fail-closed realism gate to the scalping soak acceptance/verifier path so high-sample perfect-win/no-drawdown paper artifacts are flagged as insufficient proof instead of accepted as production-quality evidence. Acceptance: verifier and scalping-soak command fail on suspicious perfect-win artifacts by default, allow small-sample smoke tests, provide an explicit documented opt-out for diagnostic runs, and include regression tests.

title: Add rollback/cleanup when buildStrategyComponents fails in bootstrap
description: CRITICAL: bootstrap.go Build() calls buildRiskComponents then buildStrategyComponents sequentially. If buildStrategyComponents fails after risk components are already registered in the actor system and supervisor, there is no rollback — the risk actor continues running in the background. Fix: add defer-based cleanup in Build() that stops/tears down already-started components if a later step fails, or restructure to use a transactional bootstrap pattern.

title: Unify routes.go kill switch/safe mode with bootstrap Application instances
description: CRITICAL: routes.go:1075 creates isolated sharedKillSwitch/apprisk.NewKillSwitch() and sharedSafeMode/apprisk.NewSafeMode() instances that are wired into AgentControlHandler via RiskControllerAdapter. These are completely separate from bootstrap.go's Application.KillSwitch and Application.SafeMode used by the RiskActor. When an operator engages the kill switch via POST /api/v1/agent/kill-switch, it only affects the route-layer instance — the RiskActor and trading pipeline continue unaffected. Fix: pass bootstrap's KillSwitch and SafeMode through to SetupRoutes (or via IntegratedHandlers) so there is a single source of truth for risk state.

title: PR1: Platform Foundation (Actor-Based Architecture)
description:
Implements PR1 (Platform Foundation) of the actor-based architecture refactor plan.

## Summary
Establishes foundational layers for converting NeuraTrade to an actor-based architecture with:
- No shared mutable state across subsystems
- Structured concurrency (every goroutine is supervised + cancellable)
- Bounded queues (backpressure) and timeouts on every IO

## Changes

### Platform Layer (internal/platform/)
- supervisor: errgroup-based lifecycle management with graceful shutdown
- actor: bounded mailboxes with overflow strategies (block/drop/reject)
- eventbus: in-process pub/sub with wildcard topic support
- timeout: standardized timeout utilities for all IO operations
- retry: exponential backoff with jitter and retry policies

### Ports Layer (internal/ports/)
- exchange: MarketDataGateway and TradingGateway contracts
- state: Repository interfaces for positions, orders, trades, signals
- notifier: Notification and alerting interfaces
- plugin: Indicator, strategy, and risk model plugin contracts
- policy: Policy engine and kill switch interfaces

### Adapters Layer (internal/adapters/)
- ccxt: Wraps existing ccxt-service to implement exchange ports

### Bootstrap (internal/app/bootstrap/)
- Application builder for dependency injection and lifecycle management

## Deliverables
- [x] platform/supervisor package
- [x] platform/actor package with bounded mailboxes
- [x] platform/eventbus package
- [x] platform/timeout and platform/retry utilities
- [x] ports/exchange, ports/state, ports/notifier interfaces
- [x] adapters/ccxt implementation
- [x] app/bootstrap wiring
- [x] Unit tests for all platform packages
- [x] Lint and build passing
- [x] PR created to development branch

Refs: docs/Refactor.md Phase 1, docs/4-level.md PR1

title: Migration Architecture & Design Document
design:
## Migration Strategy: TypeScript to Go

### Current Architecture
- **ccxt-service** (Bun/TypeScript): ~7.3K LOC, CCXT wrapper with HTTP + gRPC interfaces
- **telegram-service** (Bun/TypeScript): ~51 files, grammY bot with HTTP + gRPC interfaces
- **backend-api** (Go): Primary API server, already has gRPC clients to both services

### Recommended Approach

#### Phase 1: CCXT Service Migration (HIGH PRIORITY)
**Rationale**: Exchange API access is performance-critical, benefits most from Go's concurrency

**Options**:
1. **CCXT Go v4** (github.com/ccxt/ccxt/go/v4)
   - Pros: 1:1 API compatibility, 100+ exchanges, transpiled from TypeScript
   - Cons: Large binary, less idiomatic Go, WebSocket support maturing
   
2. **GoCryptoTrader** (github.com/thrasher-corp/gocryptotrader)
   - Pros: Native Go, production-proven, robust WebSocket, built-in rate limiting
   - Cons: Different API structure, requires full rewrite

**Recommendation**: Start with CCXT Go v4 for rapid migration, evaluate GoCryptoTrader for WebSocket features

#### Phase 2: Telegram Service (OPTIONAL)
**Rationale**: I/O-bound, not performance-critical, TypeScript is adequate

**Options**:
1. **go-telegram/bot** (github.com/go-telegram/bot)
   - Pros: Zero-dependency, extremely active (Feb 2026 updates), idiomatic Go
   - Cons: Newer library, smaller community
   
2. **telebot v4** (github.com/tucnak/telebot)
   - Pros: Best DX, 4.5k stars, grammY-like middleware
   - Cons: v4 still in beta

**Recommendation**: Keep TypeScript unless there's a compelling reason to migrate

#### Phase 3: External-Facing Components (KEEP IN TYPESCRIPT)
- TUI applications
- Webhook endpoints (if any)
- Frontend dashboards

### Technical Considerations
- Existing gRPC contracts (protos) remain unchanged
- HTTP API endpoints maintain backward compatibility
- Redis/PostgreSQL infrastructure already in Go
- Existing Go patterns: Gin, viper config, zaplogrus logging

title: Evaluate Telegram Bot Go Libraries
design:
## Task: Evaluate Telegram Bot Go Libraries

### Research Completed (Feb 2026)

**Top Recommendations**:

1. **go-telegram/bot** (github.com/go-telegram/bot) - RECOMMENDED
   - Stars: 1.6k+
   - Activity: EXTREME (v1.19.0, Feb 18 2026)
   - Pros: Zero-dependency, idiomatic Go, full Bot API 9.4 support
   - Cons: Newer than alternatives
   - Best for: Long-term stability, latest Telegram features

2. **telebot v4** (github.com/tucnak/telebot)
   - Stars: 4.5k+
   - Activity: HIGH (v4 in beta)
   - Pros: Best DX, grammY-like middleware, polished markup builder
   - Cons: v4 still in beta
   - Best for: Developer experience, rapid development

3. **gotgbot** (github.com/PaulSonOfLars/gotgbot)
   - Stars: 680+
   - Activity: HIGH (autogenerated API)
   - Pros: Complete API coverage, python-telegram-bot inspired
   - Cons: Less idiomatic Go

### Feature Comparison with grammY
| Feature | grammY | go-telegram/bot | telebot |
|---------|--------|-----------------|---------|
| Middleware | Native | Native | Native |
| Webhooks | Excellent | Built-in helper | Built-in |
| Inline Keyboards | InlineKeyboard | models.InlineKeyboardMarkup | ReplyMarkup builder |
| Rate Limiting | Plugin | Built-in 429 error types | Custom middleware |
| Session/State | Plugin | Custom implementation | Custom implementation |

### Migration Challenges
1. **State Management**: grammY's session plugin is powerful. Need to implement Redis/Postgres session store in Go.
2. **Concurrency**: Moving from Node.js event loop to goroutines (improvement for heavy tasks).
3. **API Mapping**: 1:1 mapping for most methods (sendMessage, editMessageText, etc.).

### Deliverables
- [ ] Test go-telegram/bot with our bot commands
- [ ] Test telebot v4 with our bot commands
- [ ] Implement session management pattern
- [ ] Decision document

### References
- go-telegram/bot: https://github.com/go-telegram/bot
- telebot: https://github.com/tucnak/telebot

title: Evaluate CCXT Go vs GoCryptoTrader
design:
## Task: Evaluate CCXT Go vs GoCryptoTrader

### Research Completed (Feb 2026)

**CCXT Go v4** (github.com/ccxt/ccxt/go/v4):
- Released: February 2025 (public)
- Exchange coverage: 100+ (same as TypeScript)
- Status: REST-only, WebSocket maturing
- Latest: v4.5.39 (actively maintained)
- Migration effort: LOW (1:1 API compatibility)

**GoCryptoTrader** (github.com/thrasher-corp/gocryptotrader):
- Maturity: HIGH (industry standard)
- Exchange coverage: ~50 major exchanges
- Status: Native Go, robust WebSocket
- Features: Rate limiting, gRPC server, portfolio management
- Migration effort: MEDIUM (full rewrite required)

### Evaluation Criteria
1. **Exchange Coverage**: Does it support all exchanges we currently use?
   - Current: Binance, Bybit, OKX, Coinbase, Kraken, etc.
   
2. **WebSocket Support**: Required for real-time market data?
   - CCXT Go: Limited
   - GoCryptoTrader: Full support

3. **Performance**: Latency, memory footprint
   - CCXT Go: Transpiled, larger binary
   - GoCryptoTrader: Native Go, optimized

4. **Maintenance**: Active development, community support
   - Both: Very active

### Deliverables
- [ ] Test CCXT Go v4 with our exchange list
- [ ] Test GoCryptoTrader with our exchange list
- [ ] Benchmark comparison (latency, memory)
- [ ] Decision document with recommendation

### References
- CCXT Go Issue: https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/issues/25173
- GoCryptoTrader: https://github.com/thrasher-corp/gocryptotrader

title: Fix server startup: HTTP server not starting - hanging during market data collection
description:
Root cause identified: collector.go line 654 uses PostgreSQL-specific syntax ANY() with string array, but SQLite doesn't support this. Query fails silently (logged as error but doesn't crash), preventing workers from being created, so dataReadyChan is never signaled, WaitForFirstData times out after 2 minutes, but then server should continue... 

Actually WaitForFirstData times out after 2 min but logs show it hangs forever, so something else is blocking. Need to add better logging to trace where exactly it hangs.

The fix requires either:
1. Use SQLite-compatible query syntax (e.g., WHERE e.name IN (...))
2. Or detect database type and use different queries

close_reason: Fixed in startup-orchestrator.sh by adding a backend port-listener fallback after pid-file cleanup: if backend.pid is missing/stale/removed, stop now inspects the configured BACKEND_HOST_PORT/PORT listener and only terminates it when the command matches neuratrade-server. Added services/backend-api/scripts/startup-orchestrator_test.sh with a fake neuratrade-server TCP listener and no backend.pid to prove stop removes the listener without relying on a pid file; wired into make test-scripts. Real isolated runtime smoke also passed on port 58084: startup-orchestrator start reached /ready, lsof showed neuratrade-server listening, startup-orchestrator stop returned success despite 'backend.pid is invalid' warning, and follow-up lsof/curl confirmed no listener and /health unreachable. title: Reduce hold ratio in longer scalping soak windows
description: During PR #374 continuation on 2026-05-17, the 12-cycle public Bitget no-order soak passed the broken-live baseline gates, but a longer 30-cycle operator soak failed the new MAX_HOLD_RATIO=0.745 acceptance gate. Command used services/backend-api/scripts/scalping-soak.sh with CYCLES=30, INTERVAL_MS=1000, CAPITAL=48, MIN_WIN_RATE=0.123, MIN_NET_PNL=0, MIN_SIGNAL_QUALITY_COVERAGE=1, MAX_HOLD_RATIO=0.745, MAX_AI_PROVIDER_DEGRADED_CYCLES=0. Result: acceptance gate failed with action_split.hold=0.796875 above maximum=0.745. SQLite evidence from /tmp/neuratrade-scalping-soak-long-1778998028.db: action counts buy=3, sell=36, hold=153 over 192 telemetry rows; regime counts chop=79, neutral=40, trend=73; all chop rows held, hold reasons were missing_orderbook_signal=79 and no_directional_edge=74. PnL was healthy (realized_pnl_journal count=39, wins=39, losses=0, net realized PnL ~0.46892255 USDT, fees ~0.05616603), so the remaining issue is sustained hold-heavy behavior over longer windows rather than immediate paper profitability. Acceptance: a longer no-order public Bitget soak (>=30 cycles, same 48 USDT capital and baseline gates) passes MAX_HOLD_RATIO<=0.745 without weakening signal-quality coverage, AI provider degradation, net PnL, avg PnL, win-rate, or drawdown gates; if market regime legitimately warrants high holds, document a statistically defensible longer-window gate policy distinct from the broken-live baseline.

title: Keep native gateway alive after successful paper-only startup
description: During NeuraTrade-39j runtime verification on 2026-05-13, services/backend-api/scripts/startup-orchestrator.sh started bin/neuratrade gateway start against an isolated SQLite NEURATRADE_HOME on PORT=58180. The orchestrator observed backend /health as reachable and reported success, but the gateway process exited immediately afterward. This reproduced both with default Telegram startup and with NEURATRADE_GATEWAY_SKIP_TELEGRAM=true; follow-up curl to /health failed and ps showed the gateway PID gone. Directly starting bin/neuratrade-server with JWT_SECRET and NEURATRADE_SCALPING_AUTO_EXECUTE=false stayed up and returned /health degraded only for Telegram plus /ready true, so the backend itself is viable. Acceptance: native gateway start remains alive after successful warmup in noninteractive/background startup, skip-telegram mode is covered by regression or smoke test, and startup-orchestrator status/health does not report success for a process that immediately exits.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #374 head 05d07431; detached gateway launch verified with isolated runtime smoke and focused checks.

title: Reduce contradictory LLM hold reasoning in scalping probe
description: During the 2026-05-13 built-binary DeepSeek/Bitget ai scalping-probe run for NeuraTrade-39j, one hold decision reasoned that FARTCOIN spread was above 0.22%, then immediately corrected itself that 0.085% is below 0.22%, and still held despite acknowledging strong buy imbalance and tradable spread. This did not fail the current gates because the 3-cycle window had one actionable/winning paper trade, but contradictory hold reasoning can hide missed entries and weaken recovery from the broken-live baseline hold-heavy behavior. Acceptance: add prompt/validation or diagnostics so contradictory liquidity-threshold reasoning is surfaced or reduced; cover with regression tests or a deterministic fixture; ensure healthy all-hold/hold-heavy windows remain machine-checkable via actionability gates.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #374 head 4fdc9d77: scalping LLM prompt now guards spread-threshold reasoning, probe JSON surfaces reasoning_diagnostics for contradictory hold spread claims, and regression tests cover both prompt text and deterministic diagnostic detection.

title: Normalize actionable scalping LLM reason categories
description: Built-binary PR #372 ai scalping-probe on 2026-05-13 produced an actionable ONDO/USDT buy decision with action=buy, confidence=0.65, pre_trade_gate_allowed=true, but decision.reason_category and runtime_diagnostics.last_reason_category were strategy_hold because successful non-hold LLM decisions without an explicit category are defaulted to the hold category. title: deepsec: Fix cache-key-poisoning (2 candidates)
description:
deepsec scan found 2 candidates flagged as **cache-key-poisoning** — potential cache poisoning where attacker-controlled data could influence cache keys, causing incorrect data to be served.

**Source**: deepsec scan run `20260505172439-8736ac0c3e5845b3`
**Scanner**: cache-key-poisoning
**Severity**: High

Additionally: **non-atomic-read-delete** (1 candidate) — potential race condition in read-then-delete operations.

NeuraTrade uses Redis extensively for caching market data, trading state, and distributed locks. Cache key generation should not incorporate unsanitized user input.

**Next steps**:
1. Run `bun deepsec process` for AI investigation
2. Review Redis cache key generation patterns
3. Ensure keys are deterministic and not user-influenced
4. Fix non-atomic read-delete if confirmed

title: deepsec: Fix SSRF vulnerabilities (12 candidates)
description:
deepsec scan found 12 candidates flagged as SSRF vulnerabilities: **go-ssrf** (8) and **ssrf** (4). Server-Side Request Forgery can allow attackers to make the server issue requests to internal services or external hosts.

**Source**: deepsec scan run `20260505172439-8736ac0c3e5845b3`
**Scanners**: go-ssrf + ssrf
**Severity**: High

Likely related to CCXT exchange API calls, Polymarket CLOB requests, AI provider HTTP calls, and market data fetching. Each outbound HTTP request should validate target URLs against allowed domains.

**Next steps**:
1. Run `bun deepsec process` for AI investigation
2. Add URL allowlist validation for all outbound HTTP calls
3. Block requests to internal/private IP ranges
4. Re-validate with deepsec

title: deepsec: Fix insecure crypto usage (15 candidates)
description:
deepsec scan found 15 candidates flagged as **insecure-crypto** — potential use of weak cryptographic algorithms, insufficient key lengths, predictable IVs, or other crypto weaknesses. Also found **crypto-usage** (28 candidates) for broader crypto pattern review.

**Source**: deepsec scan run `20260505172439-8736ac0c3e5845b3`
**Scanners**: insecure-crypto (15) + crypto-usage (28)
**Severity**: High

NeuraTrade uses AES-256-GCM for API key encryption (Encryptor in internal/utils/encryption.go) and Argon2 for operator identity. The scanner may flag intentional patterns (known false positives documented in INFO.md) but AI investigation is needed to confirm.

**Next steps**:
1. Run `bun deepsec process` for AI investigation
2. Confirm whether flagged patterns are intentional (AES-256-GCM, Argon2)
3. Fix any actual weak crypto usage
4. Re-validate with deepsec

title: Deduplicate Telegram notifications: only send on state change, not every cycle
description:
## Problem
The AI trading loop sends a Telegram notification on every decision cycle, even when the decision is identical to the previous one. During risk-lock or hold states, this produces spam — the same "Risk lock active, hold" message fires every ~60 seconds with only the timestamp changing.

Example from logs:
- 19:41 SELL PORTAL/USDT (legitimate — new action)
- 19:41 AI Decision: sell (ok)
- 19:41 AI Decision: hold — risk lock (first time, useful)
- 19:43 AI Decision: hold — risk lock (duplicate)
- 19:44 AI Decision: hold — risk lock (duplicate)
- 19:45 AI Decision: hold — risk lock (duplicate)
- 19:47 AI Decision: hold — risk lock (duplicate)

## Proposed Behavior
Only send a Telegram notification when the decision **changes** from the previous cycle:
- New action vs previous (hold→buy, buy→sell, etc.) → notify
- Same action, same reason, same key factors → **suppress**
- State transition (risk lock activated, risk lock lifted) → notify
- Risk lock still active (same state) → suppress

## Acceptance Criteria
- Track last-sent notification state (action + reason category + key factors hash)
- Skip sending if current decision matches last-sent state
- Always send on: trades, risk lock activation/lift, emergency actions, errors
- Never send repeated identical hold/risk-lock messages
- Trade execution notifications ("TRADE EXECUTED") are unaffected — always send

title: Fix Telegram /status trading mode display to separate persisted live mode from confirmation progress
description:
Problem:
Telegram `/status` currently renders the trading snapshot as `Mode: LIVE (0/2 confirmations)` even after the account is already in persisted live mode. This is confusing because live mode survives restart/reinstall correctly, but the UI still shows confirmation progress text that reads like live mode is not fully active.

Why this is inconsistent:
- Backend persistence stores `mode` and `confirmations` separately in `trading_mode_states`.
- Switching to live mode resets confirmations back to 0 by design after the transition succeeds.
- `/mode` already reflects this correctly by showing plain live-mode messaging once mode is `live`.
- `/status` always formats mode as `<MODE> (<confirmations>/<required> confirmations)` regardless of whether the current mode is `dry` or `live`.

Evidence:
- `services/telegram-service/src/commands/status.ts`: `summarizeMode()` always returns `${modeLabel} (${mode.confirmations}/${mode.required_confirmations} confirmations)` and `/status` uses it in the Trading Snapshot.
- `services/telegram-service/src/commands/mode.ts`: `/mode` shows dedicated live-mode copy without confirmation progress when mode is already `live`.
- `services/backend-api/internal/services/trading_mode.go`: `SetMode()` resets confirmations to 0 after mode change, while mode state is persisted and restored from DB.
- `services/backend-api/internal/api/handlers/trading_mode_handler.go`: backend returns both `mode` and confirmation fields on every response, so the UI currently conflates execution state with transition state.
- `services/backend-api/database/migrations/070_create_trading_mode_states_table.sql`: confirms persistence of trading mode state across restart/reinstall.

Reproduction:
1. Move a chat/account from dry to live mode with the required confirmations.
2. Restart the service or reinstall to verify mode persistence.
3. Run `/status`.
4. Observe `⚙️ Trading Snapshot` showing `Mode: LIVE (0/2 confirmations)`.
5. Compare with `/mode`, which presents live mode as active rather than as an in-progress confirmation state.

Expected behavior:
- `/status` should present persisted live mode as clearly live.
- Confirmation progress should only appear when it is actually relevant to a pending transition to live mode.
- The UI should distinguish execution mode from confirmation/arming state instead of compressing both into one string.

Suggested fix direction:
- Treat `mode` as the durable execution state shown in `/status`.
- Show confirmation progress only for `dry` mode when the user is accumulating confirmations toward live mode, or expose it as a separate field/line such as `Live switch confirmations: 1/2`.
- For `live` mode, show `Mode: LIVE` (optionally with a separate line if any transition metadata is relevant).
- Add/update Telegram status tests so `live` mode no longer expects confirmation text and `dry` mode coverage still verifies pending confirmation copy.

Acceptance criteria:
1. `/status` no longer shows `LIVE (0/2 confirmations)` for accounts already in live mode.
2. `/status` still surfaces confirmation progress when the account is in dry mode and confirmations are relevant to a pending switch.
3. `/status` and `/mode` present a consistent state model for dry vs live trading mode.
4. Tests cover both persisted live mode and pending-confirmation dry mode behavior.

title: Investigate /status showing entry_attempt_block_reason=max_concurrent_positions_reached for micro accounts
description: User report: /status shows entry_attempt_block_reason=max_concurrent_positions_reached and next_unblock_condition=Reduce open positions below 1 while the account tier is micro, wallet basis is about 48.54 USDT, and only one position is open with typical margin usage around 0.6-8 USDT. Investigate whether the autonomous runtime is applying an overly conservative fixed concurrent-position cap for micro accounts, whether /status messaging is missing context about why the cap is 1, and whether the cap should become adaptive based on free collateral, position sizing, confidence, risk expectancy, or other safety signals. Deliverables: trace the current logic, clarify whether this is expected behavior, and propose or implement a safer capital-efficiency improvement if warranted.
notes: Investigation notes: `/status` and Telegram diagnostics currently surface `entry_attempt_block_reason`, `next_unblock_condition_current`, `account_tier`, `effective_max_capital_pct`, `wallet_basis_usdt`, and `managed_open_positions_effective`, but they do not expose `effective_max_concurrent_positions`. The quest checkpoint persists `effective_max_concurrent_positions` in `services/backend-api/internal/services/quest_handlers_integrated.go`, but `services/backend-api/internal/services/quest_engine.go` does not aggregate that field into `GetChatRuntimeDiagnostics`, so the value never reaches `services/backend-api/internal/api/handlers/autonomous.go` or `services/telegram-service/src/commands/status.ts`. Current autonomy policy hard-caps micro accounts to 1 concurrent position in `services/backend-api/internal/app/autonomy/scalping_cycle.go` via `DefaultMicroMaxConcurrentPosition = 1` and `policy.MaxConcurrentPositions = cfg.MicroMaxConcurrent`. The entry rejection is enforced in `services/backend-api/internal/services/ai_scalping.go` when `portfolio.OpenPositions >= policy.MaxConcurrentPositions`. This means a ~49 USDT micro account with one open position will always report `max_concurrent_positions_reached` unless env override `NEURATRADE_SCALPING_MICRO_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS` is raised. The current policy adapts confidence and max capital sizing based on win rate, drawdown, loss streak, recovery mode, and expectancy, but it does not adapt concurrency upward based on free collateral or strong performance. Also note: the concurrency override env vars exist in code (`NEURATRADE_SCALPING_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS`, `NEURATRADE_SCALPING_MICRO_MAX_CONCURRENT_POSITIONS`) but are not documented in `.env.example`, which makes this behavior harder for operators to discover and tune.

title: Stabilize scalping confidence reporting during runtime degradation
description:
## Problem
Scalping hold digests currently show `Confidence: ⚪ N/A (runtime-degraded)` whenever the runtime marks confidence as unknown. In practice this is frequently triggered by state-drift gating and reconcile health, so operators lose visibility into whether the market/strategy layer still had a valid confidence estimate or whether the runtime itself was simply unsafe to execute.

## Evidence
- `services/backend-api/internal/services/quest_handlers_integrated.go`: the state-drift gate emits a hold decision with `ReasonCategory=execution_unavailable`, `Confidence=0`, and `ConfidenceKnown=false`, plus the unblock message `Require 2 consecutive clean reconcile passes with zero stale lifecycle rows`.
- `services/backend-api/internal/services/ai_scalping.go`: runtime reason categories explicitly zero confidence and mark it unknown; `runtimeDegradedHoldDecision()` also returns `ConfidenceKnown=false`.
- `services/backend-api/internal/services/notification_ops_alerts.go`: when `ConfidenceKnown` is false, the Telegram digest renders `**Confidence:** ⚪ N/A (runtime-degraded)`.
- `services/backend-api/internal/services/quest_handlers_integrated.go`: `holdDigestSummary()` maps `execution_unavailable` to `Hold digest: AI runtime degraded, waiting for stable decisioning`, which is accurate but conflates runtime health with confidence availability.

## Why this matters
This is not just a presentation bug. The system intentionally erases confidence during runtime-degraded holds, which makes it hard to distinguish:
1. no qualified setup / low-confidence strategy holds
2. valid strategy view but execution paused by state drift or reconcile health
3. true AI runtime failures (timeout/parse/circuit-open)

That makes incident triage and recovery harder, especially when the unblock condition is operational (`clean reconcile passes`) rather than model-related.

## Best fix direction
1. Split runtime health from decision confidence in the notification contract:
   - keep `Confidence`/`ConfidenceKnown` for strategy confidence
   - add a separate runtime-health/status field for `execution_unavailable`, state drift, circuit-open, etc.
2. Preserve or derive a safe non-actionable confidence signal during degraded holds when the strategy layer still has one available (for example last valid pre-gate confidence or deterministic fallback confidence), while keeping `action=hold`.
3. Tighten state-drift stabilization so the gate clears predictably:
   - add richer telemetry for stale lifecycle row IDs/counts and reconcile pass progress
   - ensure force-repair / cleanup paths explain why clean passes are not advancing
   - keep the unblock condition operator-visible
4. Keep true runtime failures (`llm_timeout`, `llm_parse_contract`, unrecoverable `execution_unavailable`) visibly degraded, but stop using the same `N/A` semantics for every non-strategy hold.
5. Add hysteresis/graded fallback semantics instead of a binary known/unknown drop where possible.

## Acceptance criteria
- Digests distinguish `strategy hold` from `runtime unavailable` and `state drift reconcile` holds.
- Runtime-health information is shown explicitly without overwriting valid confidence data when available.
- State-drift blocked -> clean reconcile recovery is covered by tests, including the 2-pass unlock behavior.
- Notification tests cover the new degraded/runtime-health semantics.
- Operators can tell from one digest whether they are waiting on market conditions, AI runtime recovery, or lifecycle reconciliation.

## Likely implementation areas
- `services/backend-api/internal/services/ai_scalping.go`
- `services/backend-api/internal/services/quest_handlers_integrated.go`
- `services/backend-api/internal/services/notification_ops_alerts.go`
- `services/backend-api/internal/services/quest_handlers_integrated_test.go`

design:
## Epic: Migrate Telegram Service to Go (OPTIONAL)

### ⚠️ Strategic Decision Required

**Recommendation**: KEEP TypeScript unless there's a compelling reason to migrate.

### Rationale
1. **Not Performance-Critical**: Telegram bot is I/O-bound, not compute-intensive
2. **grammY is Excellent**: Well-maintained, great DX, TypeScript-first
3. **Migration Cost**: ~51 files, extensive command handlers, session management
4. **Go Alternatives**: Mature but require rewriting proven code

### When to Consider Migration
- Team wants single-language codebase (Go only)
- Need tighter integration with Go backend
- Performance issues with Bun runtime (unlikely)
- Developer preference for Go

### If Proceeding: Target Architecture

- **Location**: services/telegram-service/
- **Files**: 51 TypeScript files
- **Dependencies**: grammy, hono, @grpc/grpc-js, effect
- **Features**: Commands, sessions, rate limiting, gRPC delivery

### Recommended Library: go-telegram/bot
- Zero-dependency, idiomatic Go
- Extremely active maintenance (Feb 2026 updates)
- Full Bot API 9.4 support
- Built-in error handling with retry support

### Migration Phases (If Proceeding)
1. Library evaluation (neura-rnx6)
2. Implementation (neura-3u71)
3. Testing and parallel run
